item.title: aframe-3d-model
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
aframe-3d-model

Embeds an A-Frame <a-scene> (WebXR enabled) that loads a glTF/GLB model with orbit controls, auto-rotation and damping.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — URL of the glTF/GLB model
class string no aframe-3d-model Custom class on the wrapper
style string no — Inline CSS for the wrapper
autorotate bool no true Auto-rotate the model
minDistance int no 2 Orbit controls minimum distance
maxDistance int no 10 Orbit controls maximum distance
initialPosition string no 0 0.5 4 Initial camera position
xrMode bool no true Enable the WebXR mode UI

Example

{{< aframe-3d-model src="/models/example.glb" maxDistance="20" >}}

Live demo

Loads the example model from the 3D model manifest post:

item.title: audioplayer
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
audioplayer

Renders an audio player placeholder (div.audioplayer with a play button) initialized by the audioplayer() JS function.

Note: this shortcode is marked untested — the build logs a warnf whenever it is used.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
src string yes Audio file URL, passed to the JS player
autoplay bool no Read but currently unused by the template

Example

{{< audioplayer src="audio/recording.mp3" >}}

Live demo

Plays the example audio file from static/audio/:

item.title: bibtex
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
bibtex

Intended to convert a BibTeX file (a page resource) into structured output for citations.

Note: This shortcode is not working yet — it intentionally fails the build with an errorf when used, so the site doesn’t silently render broken citations.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
file string yes — Path of the BibTeX page resource

Example

{{< bibtex file="references.bib" >}}

item.title: browser-banner
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
browser-banner

Renders a hidden banner that the browserBanner() JS function shows only when the visitor’s browser matches one of the given names. The banner is attached to the element matching parent at runtime.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
browser string no — Comma-separated list of browser names (also used as CSS classes)
class string no — Additional classes
style string no — Additional inline styles
parent string no body CSS selector the banner is appended to

The inner content is the banner text (markdownified).

item.title: browser-hide-selector
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
browser-hide-selector

Emits an inline script calling browserDisableSelector(selector, browsers): any DOM element matching selector is hidden or disabled for the listed browsers.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
selector string no "" CSS selector of the elements to hide
browser string no — Comma-separated list of browser names

Example

{{< browser-hide-selector selector=".webkit-only" browser="firefox" >}}

Live demo

The second paragraph below is hidden in Firefox (and shown elsewhere) via the webkit-only selector:

item.title: chart
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
chart

Renders a ECharts line/bar chart from a Markdown table given in the shortcode body. The data is kept in a <pre class="chart-data"> element, so it stays available as a text fallback (also useful for search and screen readers).

The optional first line of the body can start with # followed by a JSON object with ECharts options overrides (e.g. {"type": "bar"}).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
class string no — Extra class on the <figure>
caption string no — Caption below the chart

Example

{{< chart caption="Posts per year" class="wide" >}}
# {"type": "bar", "scale": true}
| Year | Posts |
|------|-------|
| 2023 | 12    |
| 2024 | 30    |
{{< /chart >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: TS ts/shortcodes/chart.ts and SCSS scss/shortcodes/chart.scss.

item.title: code
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
code

Renders a syntax highlighted code block (Hugo’s transform.Highlight/Chroma) inside a container with a title bar, a copy-to-clipboard button and a collapse checkbox.

This page documents the shortcode; see demo/code for a live example.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
lang string no — Chroma highlighting language, disables syntax guessing
title string no — Header title of the container
class string no — Custom class name
lineNumbers bool no true Show inline, anchored line numbers
lineNumbersIDPrefix string no — Chroma lineAnchors ID prefix

The inner content is the code itself.

item.title: color-sample
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
color-sample

Renders an inline color swatch (div.color-sample), optionally showing the color code as text — mainly useful for the print edition.

oliveolive

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
color string yes — Any CSS color for the background
text string no   Label inside the swatch (markdownified)
print any no — If set, appends span.color-sample-code with the raw color value

Example

{{< color-sample color="olive" text="olive" print=true >}}

item.title: csv-chart
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
csv-chart

Renders a stacked bar chart from a CSV file (a page resource), grouped by month. Expects the columns Date and Blog and counts the entries per month and category (used for statistics like “posts per blog per month”). Months without data are filled with zeros so the time axis is continuous.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
csv string yes — Path of the CSV page resource
opts string no — JSON object with ECharts options overrides

Example

{{< csv-chart csv="stats.csv" opts='{"yAxis":{"label":"Posts"}}' >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: TS ts/shortcodes/chart.ts (shared with chart) and SCSS scss/shortcodes/csv-chart.scss.

item.title: dates/build-date
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)

dates/build-date

Renders the build/render time (now) as <date class="build-date"> using the :date_short / :time_medium layouts.

Build time: 10/23/26 7:51:07 pm

Built on {{< dates/build-date >}}

item.title: dates/lastmod
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
dates/lastmod

Renders the current page’s Lastmod date as <date class="lastmod"> using the :date_medium layout.

Last modified: Jan 1, 1

Parameters

None.

Example

Last modified: {{< dates/lastmod >}}

Note

Results may be misleading with enableGitInfo — Lastmod then reflects the last Git commit of the page.

item.title: embargo
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
embargo

Time-gated content: the inner content is rendered only when the build time is at or after the until timestamp. “Now” is corrected to the newest post’s date if any post is dated in the future (so scheduled posts don’t leak embargoed content early).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
until date no build time Timestamp the content is released at (time.AsTime syntax)

Warnings

  • warnf "Future detected!" — the newest page date lies in the future
  • warnf "Embargo broken for <path>" — an embargo has expired and its content is shown

Example

{{< embargo until="2026-12-24" >}}
Secret content, revealed on Christmas.
{{< /embargo >}}

item.title: figure
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
figure

Renders a <figure> with <img> and optional <figcaption> (based on kaushalmodi’s refined theme).

Handles three src modes: full URLs (http(s)… or //), site-absolute paths (/…, prepended with the site BaseURL) and page-relative paths (prepended with the page permalink — the default language’s permalink for translated pages).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — Image URL or path
link string no — Wrap the image in <a href>
target, rel string no — Attributes for the wrapping <a> (with link)
alt string no caption Image alt text
caption string no — Figure caption (markdownified)
title string no — Rendered as <h4> in the figcaption
width, height string no — Image dimensions
class string no — Class on the <figure>
attr string no — Attribution (markdownified)
attrlink string no — Wraps the attribution in <a href>

Example

{{< figure src="/images/cc.png" caption="Example caption" >}}

item.title: flag
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
flag

Renders a language flag image (/images/lang/<lang>.gif, provided by the site) with the localized language name as alt text.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
(positional 0) string yes — Language code, also used as i18n key for the alt text

Example

{{< flag de >}}

Assets

None.

item.title: footnote
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
footnote

Renders a superscript footnote reference (<sup id="fnref:…"> linking to #fn:…) and stores the footnote text in the page’s store for later output by footnote-list.

This is a test of the footnote shortcode1 in a page.

Parameters

Positional arguments:

Position Type Required Purpose
0 string yes Footnote ID
1 string yes Footnote text (markdownified)

Example

Some text{{< footnote 1 "The footnote text." >}} continues here.

item.title: footnote-list
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
footnote-list

Renders the footnotes collected by footnote (stored in the page’s store) as a div.footnotes with an ordered list, each entry carrying a back-reference (↩︎). Deletes the store afterwards — use it once per page, after the footnotes.

Renders nothing when no footnotes were collected.

Parameters

None.

Example

Text with a note{{< footnote 1 "The footnote text." >}}.

…

{{< footnote-list >}}

item.title: gallery
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
gallery

Renders an image gallery with a PhotoSwipe lightbox. The shortcode body is a JSON array of image definitions; images are loaded as page resources. A small WebP preview is generated (scalePreview can turn this off), captions are hidden visually and shown in the lightbox.

Images with .hdr. in their filename link to the HDR image on the default language’s page instead of opening the lightbox.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
class string no — Extra class on the gallery <div>

Body (JSON array)

Property Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — Page resource path of the image
alt string no "" Image alt text and lightbox caption (also used for aria-label)
scalePreview bool no true Generate a resized WebP preview

Example

{{< gallery >}}
[
  { "src": "image-1.jpg", "alt": "First image" },
  { "src": "image-2.jpg", "alt": "Second image", "scalePreview": false }
]
{{< /gallery >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: JS ts/shortcodes/gallery.ts, SCSS scss/shortcodes/gallery.scss and the PhotoSwipe stylesheet.

item.title: hdr-canvas
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
hdr-canvas

Renders an image on a HDR capable canvas with red/green/blue channel sliders for colour manipulation. Requires a browser with HDR canvas support; on unsupported browsers a hidden fallback message is shown to screen readers and the image is displayed as SDR.

item.title: hdr-model
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
hdr-model

Renders a glTF/GLB model on a canvas using three.js with a HDR WebGPU renderer (falling back to WebGL) and orbit controls with auto-rotation. For an alternative implementation using A-Frame see aframe-3d-model, for the non HDR variant see model.

On translated pages the model URL is prefixed with the default language’s permalink.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
model string yes — URL of the glTF/GLB model

Example

{{< hdr-model model="model/example.glb" >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: TS ts/shortcodes/hdr-model.ts and SCSS scss/shortcodes/hdr-model.scss.

item.title: html/comment
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/comment

Outputs the inner content wrapped in an HTML comment (<!-- … -->) — useful to keep notes in the published HTML or to disable markup.

Parameters

None (inner content only).

Example

{{< html/comment >}}This text is only visible in the page source.{{< /html/comment >}}

item.title: html/div
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/div

Wraps content in a plain <div class="…"> — a workaround for Markdown’s inability to group block elements with classes.

Content inside a classed div.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
class string no Class attribute of the div
content string no Div body as raw string, overrides the inner content

Example

{{< html/div class="note" >}}Content inside a classed div.{{< /html/div >}}

item.title: html/iframe-consent
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/iframe-consent

GDPR consent wrapper for embedded iframes: renders an overlay (“external content” notice via i18n externalContent/externalContentDescription) with a toggle switch (i18n accept). Accepting stores a consent cookie (30 days, keyed by an md5 of the iframe markup) and loads the iframe — until then only the optional preview is shown. With JavaScript enabled the checkbox fallback is replaced by a real <button role="switch" aria-checked> (via ts/iframe-consent.ts, loaded automatically); a stored consent is applied on reload without interaction.

item.title: html/include
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/include

Includes the content of an external HTML file — everything between its <body>…</body> — inside a div.included-html. The path is resolved relative to the page’s file directory via the partial html/html-body.html, see shortcode helper: file includes.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
file string yes Path relative to the page directory

Example

{{< html/include file="extra.html" >}}

Errors

Inherited from html/html-body.html:

  • errorf "Can't find <file>!" — file doesn’t exist
  • errorf "…Contents of <file> is nil…" / errorf "<file> is either empty!" — unusable content
  • errorf "Cant find context or src in…" — called with unusable arguments

item.title: html/link
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/link

Renders a download link (div.download-link with a.<class>, target="_blank") to a file relative to the page permalink — without any existence check (see html/link-if-exists for the checked variant).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
file string yes — Path relative to the page
content string no the file value Link text
class string no link Class on the <a>

Example

{{< html/link file="attachment.pdf" content="Download (PDF)" >}}

item.title: html/link-if-exists
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/link-if-exists

Renders a download link (div.download-link with a.link, target="_blank") to a file relative to the page permalink — but only if the file actually exists on disk. Otherwise nothing is rendered.

See html/link for the variant without the existence check.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
file string yes Path relative to the page
content string no Link text, defaults to the file value

Example

{{< html/link-if-exists file="attachment.pdf" content="Download (PDF)" >}}

Warnings

  • warnf "File <absolute path> doesn't exist!" — logged when the file is missing (nothing rendered)

item.title: html/rawhtml
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
html/rawhtml

Bypasses Hugo’s Markdown sanitization by emitting the inner content verbatim, preceded by an <!-- raw html --> comment (the anaulin.org raw HTML shortcode pattern). Useful when Markdown mangles otherwise valid HTML.

Parameters

None (inner content only).

Example

{{< html/rawhtml >}}
<details><summary>Click me</summary>Raw HTML content</details>
{{< /html/rawhtml >}}

item.title: iiif/iiif
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
iiif/iiif

Embeds a single image via the IIIF Image API using the OpenLayers based viewer: a uniquely named map div loading the info.json, with an optional share bar (download/manifest/page links).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — URL of the image’s info.json
share any no false Show share/download links
hdr any no false Enable HDR support in the viewer
downloadURL string no — Link target for the full-resolution download

Example

{{< iiif/iiif src="https://iiif.example.org/page0001/info.json" share="true" >}}

Live demo

Loads an Image API 2 info.json from the Blaufußtölpel blog with the share bar enabled:

item.title: iiif/presentation

iiif/presentation

Embeds a Presentation API manifest using the configured viewer (TIFY by default, see IIIF configuration): a div.iiif > div.viewer.presentation-api initialized by iiifPresentationViewer() with the manifest URL.

The manifest URL is resolved relative to the page permalink (translation-aware, .html stripped).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose

Example

{{< iiif/presentation manifestUrl="subdir/manifest.json" >}}

Live demo

Loads the Presentation 3 manifest generated by this example site itself — the path is relative to this page’s URL:

item.title: image-compare
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
image-compare

Renders a before/after image comparison slider based on the img-comparison-slider Web Component. Both images are loaded as page bundle resources and resized to a 1280 px width.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
image1 string yes Page resource path of the first (before) image
image2 string yes Page resource path of the second (after) image
caption1 string no Caption and alt text for the first image
caption2 string no Caption and alt text for the second image

item.title: link
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
link

Renders an <a> element around the inner content. External URLs (starting http or // and not pointing at the site BaseURL) automatically get the class external and target="_blank".

An internal link: to the shortcode section . An external one: IIIF .

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
link string no Href value (without it the <a> has no href)
title string no Title attribute
class string no Additional classes (merged with external)

The inner content is the link text.

item.title: list-tag-posts
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
list-tag-posts

Renders a ul.tagged-posts list of pages from a section carrying the given tag(s). When multiple tags are given (via tags), all of them must match. The current page is excluded.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
tag string no — Single tag to match
tags string no — Comma-separated tag list, overrides tag
section string no post Section to search

Example

{{< list-tag-posts tag="iiif" section="post" >}}

See also the tag cloud demo for tag related demos.

item.title: lucienne
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
lucienne

Embeds the Lucienne IIIF playground viewer (div.lucienne-container), initialized with an IIIF source URL — optionally overridden by a ?url= query parameter. Lucienne offers a URL input, resizing, download and shift navigation.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — Initial IIIF source URL (errorf when missing)
class string no — Currently read but not emitted
urlinput / urlInput bool no false Show the URL input field
resize bool no true Allow resizing
download bool no true Show download option
useLocation / uselocation bool no false Sync with the browser location (note the case sensitivity quirk between the two spellings)
autoLoad bool no true Load the initial source automatically
shifts bool no false Enable shift navigation

Example

{{< lucienne src="https://iiif.example.org/manifest.json" urlinput="true" >}}

Live demo

Loads the Presentation 3 manifest generated by this example site itself:

item.title: maps/osm
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
maps/osm

Renders an OpenStreetMap container for OpenLayers: div.map-wrapper.script with a div.map and a popup div, then an inline script calling window.initMap(id, geojsonURL, 'osm', cluster[, marker]) followed by updateSize(). The actual logic lives in the partial maps/osm.html; the shortcode is a thin wrapper.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — URL/path of the GeoJSON source
cluster any no false Enable point clustering
marker any no false Marker configuration, passed through to the OpenLayers icon style

Example

{{< maps/osm src="/geojson/places.geojson" cluster="true" >}}

Live demo

Loads the example GeoJSON from static/geojson/ with clustering enabled:

item.title: maps/osm-vector-tiles
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
maps/osm-vector-tiles

Renders an OpenStreetMap vector tile map using OpenLayers with an ol-mapbox-style compatible style: div.map-wrapper.script with a div.map and a popup div, then an inline script calling window.projektemacherMap(...). The logic lives in ts/maps/ (mapWrapper.ts / projektemacher-map.ts).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
src string yes — URL/path of the GeoJSON source
style string yes — Mapbox style — either an asset path (resolved via resources.Get, inlined) or a URL (loaded client side)
source string no from style Tile URL overriding the style’s source, e.g. https://tiles.versatiles.org/tiles/osm/{z}/{x}/{y}
marker string no undefined OpenLayers icon options as JavaScript object literal, e.g. {src: '/images/map-marker.svg', scale: 0.1, anchor: [0.5, 1], anchorXUnits: 'fraction', anchorYUnits: 'fraction'}. SVG sources are supported and recommended for markers that scale with the cluster size
cluster any no false Cluster point features; clicking a cluster either zooms in or shows a merged popup. With a marker set, icon size grows with the number of members: scale × (1 + clusterScaleFactor·log₂(n)), capped at clusterScaleMax × scale; the size badge scales along. Optional marker keys clusterScaleFactor (default 0.25) and clusterScaleMax (default 3) tune this
bbox string no undefined Bounding box [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]
center string no undefined Map center [lon, lat], defaults to the GeoJSON center

Unlike maps/osm this shortcode renders vector tiles via ol-mapbox-style — the style parameter expects a Mapbox style JSON, not a tile layer name.

item.title: model
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
model

Renders a glTF/GLB model on a canvas using three.js with orbit controls, auto-rotation and an optional halftone postprocessing effect. For the HDR/WebGPU variant see hdr-model, for the A-Frame variant see aframe-3d-model.

The canvas is exposed to assistive technology with role="img" and a localized aria-label.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
model string yes — URL of the glTF/GLB model

Example

{{< model model="model/example.glb" >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: TS ts/shortcodes/model.ts, SCSS scss/shortcodes/model.scss.

item.title: pdf
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
pdf

Renders a PDF viewer container (div.pdf-viewer) initialized by the global addPDFViewer() JS function, plus an optional download link. The path is relative to the page permalink.

JS ts/pdf-viewer.ts and SCSS scss/pdf-viewer.scss are loaded automatically via the shortcode metadata.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
file string yes — PDF path relative to the page
download string no true Set to anything but true to hide the download link

Example

{{< pdf file="document.pdf" >}}

Live demo

Loads the demo.pdf page resource of this page:

item.title: pdf-preview
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
pdf-preview

Embeds an inline PDF preview via PDFObject (PDFObject.embed) into a uniquely ID’d div, with a fallback notice (i18n InlinePDFNotSupported) and an optional download link (i18n pdfDownload). The path is relative to the page permalink (translation-aware).

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
pdf string yes — PDF path relative to the page (nothing rendered when empty)
page int no 1 Initial page
class string no pdf-preview Class on the container
download any no false Show the download link

Example

{{< pdf-preview pdf="document.pdf" page="2" download="true" >}}

Assets

Via the shortcode helper: JS ts/pdf-preview.ts, SCSS scss/pdf-preview.scss.

item.title: post-count
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
post-count

Outputs the number of pages in a section, optionally filtered by the front matter type parameter.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
section string yes — Section name
type string no — Filter on the pages’ type front matter

Example

There are 65 pages in this section.

item.title: post-image
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
post-image

Renders the first image from another post’s front matter resources array as a <figure>. Useful for teaser images that should stay in sync with the original post.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
post string yes — Path of the post (relative to section if given)
section string no — Section to look up the post in
width string no — Resize the image to the given width
link string no — Wrap the image in <a href>
caption string no — Figure caption, also used as image alt (falls back to the post title)
class string no — Class on the <figure>

Example

{{< post-image section="posts" post="my-post" caption="Teaser image" width="320" >}}

Assets

None.

item.title: print/env
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/env

Renders the inner content (through $.Page.RenderString) only when the Hugo environment is print — used to add content that appears exclusively in the print edition.

See the print edition shortcodes (print/*) for related shortcodes.

Parameters

None (inner content only).

Example

{{< print/env >}}This paragraph only appears in the print build.{{< /print/env >}}

item.title: print/image
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/image

Renders a <figure><img src="…"></figure> for the print edition, optionally wrapped in a link. The image path is the page path joined with src, then stripped of the first print.relative characters — a site parameter used to adjust paths for the print build’s directory layout.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
src string yes Image path relative to the page
alt string no Alt text
class string no Class on the <figure>
link string no Wraps the figure in <a href>

Site config

print.relative — path offset applied to the computed image URL (default 0).

item.title: print/pb
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/pb

Page break for the print edition: emits </div><div class="page"> to close the current page div and open the next one. Optionally renders the page’s collected footnotes (partial print/footnotes.html) before the break.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
footnotes any no If set, render the page’s footnotes at this break

Example

…end of the printed page.

{{< print/pb footnotes="true" >}}

item.title: print/qr
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/qr

Generates a QR code image at build time (Hugo’s images.QR) and renders it as an <img>; the URL is adjusted by the print.relative site parameter. The payload comes from the text parameter or the inner content.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
text string yes* — QR payload (if no inner content is given)
scale int no 4 Pixel scale of the generated image
alt string no "" Alt text
class string no "" Class on the <img>
title string no "" Title attribute

* required unless the inner content provides the payload.

item.title: print/ref
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/ref

Cross-reference for the print edition: renders <a class="page-ref" href="#_-<section>-<slug>"> pointing to the anchor of another page printed in the same document. The link text is the referenced page’s title (or its description as fallback), a custom string, or just the page abbreviation (i18n pageAbbr), suffixed with the page abbreviation.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
slug string yes — Slug of the target page below section
section string no post Section of the target page
title bool/string no — true uses the target’s title/description; a string is used verbatim; omitted → only the page abbreviation

Example

See {{< print/ref slug="introduction" title="true" >}} for details.

Errors

  • errorf "[print-ref.html] No argument given in <page>" when slug is empty

item.title: print/status
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
print/status

Renders a div.print-status block with a “generated” timestamp (i18n generated, long date + short time). In non-print environments it additionally shows the Git revision (abbreviated hash via .Page.GitInfo, i18n revision) and optional notes.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
notes string no Extra notes (markdownified), only rendered outside the print environment

Example

{{< print/status notes="Generated from the working tree" >}}

Requirements

GitInfo must be enabled for the revision display (enableGitInfo = true).

item.title: quote
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
quote

Renders a div.quote with a <blockquote class="quote-body"> and an optional div.quote-from attribution. The quote text comes from the inner content, the quote parameter or a file (in that priority).

That brain of mine is something more than merely mortal.
Ada Lovelace

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
quote string no Quote text (markdownified, overridden by inner content)
from string no Attribution line (markdownified)
file string no File whose content becomes the quote (overridden by inner content)
link string no Wraps the blockquote in <a href>
from-link string no Wraps the attribution in <a href>
source-link string no Adds a separate “source” (i18n) link after the attribution

Example

{{< quote from="Ada Lovelace" >}}
That brain of mine is something more than merely mortal.
{{< /quote >}}

item.title: related
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
related

Renders a div.related-post box with an i18n heading (relatedPosts) around the inner content (markdownified) — a visual wrapper for “related posts” notes.

Related posts

See the shortcodes overview for other shortcodes.

Parameters

None (inner content only).

Example

{{< related >}}
More about this in [another post](/post/other/).
{{< /related >}}

item.title: shell
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
shell

Renders a syntax highlighted code block (Hugo’s transform.Highlight/Chroma) as a macOS style shell window with traffic light buttons: the red and green buttons collapse (or expand) the window, the yellow button copies the raw code to the clipboard.

This page documents the shortcode; see demo/shell for a live example.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Purpose
lang string no — Chroma highlighting language, disables syntax guessing
title string no Terminal Window title in the title bar
class string no — Custom class name
lineNumbers bool no true Show inline, anchored line numbers
collapsed bool no false Render the window initially collapsed
lineNumbersIDPrefix string no — Chroma lineAnchors ID prefix

The inner content is the code itself. Copying always copies this raw content, independent of the displayed highlighting or line numbers.

item.title: Shortcode helper system
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
Shortcode helper system

Shortcodes often need page specific JavaScript and styles. This theme ships a helper system that detects which shortcodes a page uses and includes only the required assets for that page — no global asset bloat.

Declaring shortcode assets

A shortcode declares its requirements with an inline partial named _partials/shortcodes/<name>-metadata.html, returning a JSON object with css, js and/or scss lists:

{{- define "_partials/shortcodes/code-metadata.html" -}}
  {{- (dict "css" slice "js" (slice "ts/shortcodes/code.ts") "scss" (slice "scss/shortcodes/code.scss")) | jsonify -}}
{{- end -}}

Paths starting with http are treated as external resources, everything else is resolved from assets/.

item.title: tagcloud
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
tagcloud

Renders a div.tagcloud of links for the site’s tags taxonomy, sorted by count with a logarithmic font size between 12 and 48 px. Only tags used at least three times are shown; the terms hugo, tags and rss are excluded. Labels are humanized with a count badge.

This page documents the shortcode; see the tag cloud demo for a live example.

Parameters

None.

Example

{{< tagcloud >}}

Variants

tags/cloud is the customizable variant of this shortcode, rendering each label through partials.

item.title: tags/cloud
item.author: mail@christianmahnke.de (Christian Mahnke)
item.description:
tags/cloud

The customizable variant of tagcloud: same tag cloud logic, but each term label is rendered through a partial — tagcloud/tag.html by default, or tagcloud/tag-<tag>.html when the tag parameter is given. Available label partials include tag-humanize.html, tag-i18n.html, tag-page.html and tag-replace-hyphen.html.

Like tagcloud, only terms with a count ≥ 3 are shown (excluding hugo, tags, rss), with a logarithmic font size between 12 and 48 px.

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Purpose
tag string no Selects the label partial tagcloud/tag-<tag>.html

Example

{{< tags/cloud tag="i18n" >}}
